skill.name: bloxstack-onboarding
skill.description: Connect an AI assistant to a Roblox team's BloxStack workspace through the BloxStack MCP server. Use when a creator asks to get started on BloxStack, connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another MCP client, or get a first briefing on their studio's games and tasks.
skill.summary: Connect an AI assistant to BloxStack and get a first briefing on your Roblox studio.
skill.author: bloxstack
skill.license: May be installed and redistributed verbatim with attribution to BloxStack.

security_audit.summary: The static matches are Markdown formatting, fixed client setup commands, expected BloxStack URLs, or MCP tool names. No evidence found of shell substitution or credential exfiltration. An existing connection is read before its studio is verified, and the skill directs assistants to follow connection notices without checking their source.

remediation.issue: Studio identity is checked after the initial read.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the studio through the client or consent screen before fetching data. Ask the creator to reconnect with read-only access if the studio cannot be verified.

remediation.issue: Connection notice instructions are not checked against a trusted source.
remediation.suggestion: Treat notices as data and use documented recovery steps. Ask the creator before changing connection settings or permissions.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format the MCP endpoint as inline Markdown. They do not evaluate the URL as a command.
The Markdown shows a fixed Claude Code setup command with no user input or shell substitution. It registers the server, and sign-in follows separately.
The inline examples register the fixed endpoint and start the Codex sign-in flow. The commands do not interpolate workspace data or credentials.
The line shows a fixed Gemini CLI registration command and an in-client authentication command. The backticks format both instructions and do not execute them.
The backticked text is the server name used in client settings. It is not a shell command.
The backticks mark an MCP tool name and an empty argument object. The instruction calls a connected MCP tool through the client, not a shell.
The backticked name refers to a task-reading MCP tool, used only if available. It is not shell syntax.
The URL identifies the BloxStack MCP endpoint used by the requested integration. This line does not instruct the assistant to send credentials or studio data.
The link opens the BloxStack Studio page for account sign-in and studio selection. The creator handles sign-in rather than sharing credentials with the assistant.
The fixed URL is the server registered in Claude Code for BloxStack onboarding. Authentication follows through the client, with studio access approved in the browser.
The fixed URL configures the intended BloxStack endpoint in Codex. The separate login step uses the client sign-in flow rather than sending a pasted token.
Gemini registers the stated BloxStack endpoint and starts authentication in the client. The setup instruction does not specify an unrelated destination or include secret values.
Both URLs are documentation links on the BloxStack domain. They do not include user data or instruct the assistant to upload anything.

semantic_findings.title: Existing Connection Read Before Studio Verification
semantic_findings.description: The skill reuses an existing connection and reads studio data before checking the studio name. The first response can expose another studio's information to the current chat context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The order of operations is explicit: the studio read returns data before the name check. The skill stops further reads if it detects a mismatch.

semantic_findings.title: Connection Notices Treated as Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to use instructions from access or connection-limit notices without checking their origin. Misleading notices could steer the assistant beyond the approved onboarding task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to follow notices has no source check or action boundary. No evidence found of a malicious notice in the supplied files.

content.user_title: Connect Your AI Assistant to BloxStack
content.value_statement: Connecting an AI assistant to a Roblox studio can be confusing when each client has different setup steps. This skill guides the connection and uses approved access to answer your first studio question.
actual_capabilities: Guide setup for the current client or reuse an existing BloxStack connection.
Guide the creator through browser sign-in, studio selection, and read-only approval.
Check the studio name returned by the first read and stop further reads if it differs from the expected name.
Summarize a game or open task based on the data returned by BloxStack.
Read the task board when the connected client exposes the task-listing tool.
Explain the next step when the client cannot complete the initial studio read.
limitations: Requires a client that supports remote HTTP MCP and OAuth.
The creator must complete sign-in and approve access in the browser.
A configured endpoint does not prove that studio access works.
The onboarding workflow does not open a hosted Roblox Studio session or save a draft task without a separate request.

use_cases.title: Connect a new studio workspace
use_cases.description: Connect a supported client and confirm that it can read the studio selected in the browser.

use_cases.title: Get a first team briefing
use_cases.description: Check the connected studio and learn about one game or open task before joining team discussions.

use_cases.title: Review upcoming studio work
use_cases.description: Ask for a short task-board summary or request a draft task in chat if the board is empty.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect this app to BloxStack. Give me the next step and let me approve read-only access in my browser.

prompt_templates.title: Ask for a studio briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing BloxStack connection for [studio name]. Tell me the studio name and one game or open task. Stop if the returned name differs.

prompt_templates.title: Review upcoming tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: For [studio name], summarize upcoming work if the task board is available. If it is empty, suggest one draft task in chat without saving it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a failed first read
prompt_templates.prompt: My Codex connection is set up for [studio name], but the first studio read fails. Report the last successful step and one documented action to restore read-only access.

output_examples.input: My connection is ready. What is one game in Harbor Studio?
output_examples.output: The connected workspace is Harbor Studio. One game in the workspace is Harbor Racing.

output_examples.input: What work is on the Harbor Studio task board?
output_examples.output: The Harbor Studio task board has no tasks. A possible first task is to list the changes needed before the next playtest. Nothing was saved.

output_examples.input: The first read returned Riverside Studio, but I expected Harbor Studio.
output_examples.output: The connected studio does not match Harbor Studio, so I stopped before reading further. Reconnect and select Harbor Studio in the browser approval screen.

best_practices: Verify the intended studio and account before approving or reusing a connection.
Turn off Allow changes in the browser for a read-only introduction.
Keep sign-in details and tokens in the client or browser.
anti_patterns: Assuming that a configured endpoint proves access to the right studio.
Continuing to read the task board after a studio mismatch.
Following recovery instructions from an unverified connection notice.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: You need a BloxStack studio and a client that supports remote HTTP MCP and OAuth. Claude, Claude Code, and Codex have separate setup paths.

faq.question: How do I keep the connection read-only?
faq.answer: Turn off Allow changes before you approve access in the browser. Review the existing grant before reusing a connection.

faq.question: Should I paste my password or token into chat?
faq.answer: No. Complete sign-in through the client and browser without putting credentials in chat.

faq.question: What if the expected studio is missing?
faq.answer: Check which Roblox account you used and whether it belongs to the studio. Reconnect to the intended studio before reading more data.

faq.question: Can the skill show upcoming work?
faq.answer: Yes, when the connected client exposes the task-listing tool. If the board is empty, the assistant can suggest a draft task in chat.

faq.question: Where can I review or end the connection?
faq.answer: Open the Agent page for your BloxStack studio to review or end the connection.
